title: docs: MCP_SERVER.md's claim_next_task and wait_for_task sections omit the executionRoute parameter and the EXECUTION_ROUTE_REQUIRED refusal, and claim_next_task still documents an "Epic already has an active worker" error the code never raises
description:

PROBLEM AND EVIDENCE (docs/MCP_SERVER.md at 8ca8d389):
- `### moe.claim_next_task` (:1428) and `### moe.wait_for_task` (:1554) do not document the `executionRoute` input or the EXECUTION_ROUTE_REQUIRED refusal that both tools implement. See the executionRoute handling in tools/claimNextTask.ts and tools/waitForTask.ts.
- :1546 documents "`Epic already has an active worker on <status> tasks: <workerId>` - if another worker is active", an error no code path raises (grep the daemon src).

ALSO OWED. Hunt #10's rows 7d3428d1 (get_commit_scope's workerId comment), 55a5a9f9 (request_replan's Returns block, about :2880-2892) and 34e42a0a (the GLOBAL lists propose_rail can reach) were told to include a one-line MCP_SERVER.md sync only if the file was free. Check each row's completion diff, and apply any sync it skipped here.

HOW. Docs only. Edit with the seat's own editor (Claude Edit, or apply_patch on codex exec), never Serena (this checkout's .serena/project.yml ignores docs/). Stay inside the named sections.

implementationPlan.description:
Docs only. Edit `### moe.claim_next_task` in docs/MCP_SERVER.md with your own editor: Claude Edit, or apply_patch on codex exec. Never use Serena (.serena/project.yml ignores docs/), and never a shell write: a write with no TOOL witness gets the path held at landing (mem:gotcha-docs-edit-via-bash-python-no-tool-witness). Work in your task checkout (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`), never in /mnt/d/projexts/moes (mem:decision-doc-row-checkrefs-worktree-mode). The byte-exact reference for every new line is /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-a024/MCP_SERVER.sections.diff (sha256 a94dd0cb86981a18…; it applied cleanly at a3330bce). Copy the text from it or from here. Four edits:
(A) Parameters block: the `host?: string` line gains a trailing comma (comment column unchanged). Then add this line before `}`:
  executionRoute?: 'vm'            // only a Moe VM-route wrapper sends it (see "Execution route")
(B) Add one new paragraph, with a blank line on each side, between the `**Execution profile admission:**` paragraph and the `**Runner process identity (optional, both or neither):**` paragraph. It must start with the exact lead-in `**Execution route (optional):** ` because the step-3 check looks for it. Full text (reference diff, added line [3]):
**Execution route (optional):** `executionRoute` takes one value, `"vm"`. Only a wrapper that runs the seat's `WORKING` or `REVIEW` session in a Moe VM (CQ-M07m/n) sends it; every other caller omits it. Any other supplied value (`"host"`, `"VM"`, `""`, `null`, a number, an object) is refused `-32602` / `INVALID_INPUT` naming `executionRoute`, right after the runner-identity check and before any write. The marker can only refuse, and it is not authentication: it guards against an accidental host run (an older wrapper, a hand-run CLI). A `WORKING` or `REVIEW` task whose execution is strict under **Execution profile admission** (its effective profile is `verified-local`, or, on an own-seat resume, the caller's own open attempt recorded a `verified-local` snapshot) is refused to every claim without `executionRoute: "vm"`. An explicit-`taskId` claim, including one with no `workerId` and the own seat's resume, gets a thrown `-32003` / `EXECUTION_ROUTE_REQUIRED` before any write. Its message reads `[EXECUTION_ROUTE_REQUIRED] Task <id> runs under verified-local: only a VM-route seat may claim it in <status> …`, `error.data.codeName` is `EXECUTION_ROUTE_REQUIRED`, and its `context` (`{ taskId, status, executionProfile, requiredRoute }`) stays in the daemon. The ranked pool skips such a row instead. The route check runs after readiness, so the marker never satisfies or skips readiness or any other check: while `verified-local` is not ready, every claim of such a row is refused `EXECUTION_PROFILE_NOT_READY` first, with or without the marker, and `EXECUTION_ROUTE_REQUIRED` can fire only once readiness holds. A marked claim still meets the dependency gate and the finalizing hold. `PLANNING` rows (architects stay on the host) and legacy or observe rows never need the marker, and a marked claim of one is admitted exactly as an unmarked one. The `moe.wait_for_task` hints this tool answers with (no claimable task, or every candidate taken) carry `executionRoute: "vm"` in `args` only when the claim sent it, so a seat that follows the hint waits marked; an unmarked claim's hint has no `executionRoute` key.
(C) Under **Worker Constraint:**, replace the lead line `Only one worker can work on tasks of the same status type per epic at a time:` with the line below, and keep its three bullets:
For a claimer in no team (see **No team membership** below), only one worker can work on tasks of the same status type per epic at a time; a team member is not limited by it, and a candidate it rules out is skipped, never an error:
Why: the error bullet deleted in (D) was this constraint's only stated outcome. The code skips the candidate (the solo-rule `continue`) and then answers NO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP or the hasNext:false concurrent-claim hint. It never raises an error.
(D) Under **Errors:**, delete the bullet `- `Epic already has an active worker on <status> tasks: <workerId>` - if another worker is active`. A grep of the daemon, proxy, plugins and scripts finds nothing that raises it. Then append these two bullets after the `-32003 EXECUTION_PROFILE_NOT_READY` bullet:
- `-32602 INVALID_INPUT`: `executionRoute` present with any value other than `"vm"`. Raised before any write (see **Execution route**).
- `-32003 EXECUTION_ROUTE_REQUIRED`: an explicit claim without `executionRoute: "vm"` of a `WORKING` or `REVIEW` task whose execution is strict, once `verified-local` is ready. Raised before any write; the ranked pool skips such a row instead (see **Execution route**).
Touch nothing else in the section. In particular, leave the Notes bullets on firstClaimAt and fileCollision alone: task-6cf09180 (peek fix a3330bce, in REVIEW) owns any sync there.

Docs only, with the same editor and checkout rules as step 1. Edit `### moe.wait_for_task` in docs/MCP_SERVER.md. Three edits; their text is reference diff added lines [7]-[10]:
(E) Parameters block. Anchor the Edit on two lines: `  epicId?: string,      // Optional epic filter` and the `  timeoutMs?: number    // Max wait…` line under it. Another tool's block (~:3071) has the same timeoutMs line, so an old_string holding that line alone is ambiguous. The timeoutMs line becomes:
  timeoutMs?: number,   // Max wait in ms (default 300000, clamped to 1000–600000)
Then add this line before `}`:
  executionRoute?: 'vm' // only a Moe VM-route wrapper sends it; pass the same value to moe.claim_next_task
(F) Under **Notes:**, insert this bullet directly after the `- **Execution profile admission matches `claim_next_task` too:**` bullet, exactly:
- **The execution route matches `claim_next_task` too:** `executionRoute` is parsed as `claim_next_task` parses it, and the matcher hands it to the same predicate. Once `verified-local` is ready, a `WORKING` or `REVIEW` row whose execution is strict (the row `claim_next_task` refuses with `EXECUTION_ROUTE_REQUIRED`; see its **Execution route**) matches only a waiter that sent `executionRoute: "vm"`. That includes the caller's own held task: an unmarked seat parks, and a marked one wakes at once. The wait never raises `EXECUTION_ROUTE_REQUIRED` itself; it skips the row. Every re-match on `TASK_CREATED`/`TASK_UPDATED` reads the same parsed value, and the `moe.claim_next_task` hint, like the timeout's `moe.wait_for_task` hint, carries `executionRoute: "vm"` in `args` only when the wait sent it, so the claim reads the same predicate with the same route.
(G) Under **Errors:**, append this bullet after `- `[MISSING_REQUIRED] Missing required field: workerId``:
- `[INVALID_INPUT] Invalid executionRoute: must be 'vm' when present` — `executionRoute` present with any other value (`null`, `""` and `"VM"` included); raised after the `statuses` presence check, before every other check and before any waiter is registered
Source facts: waitForTask.ts calls parseExecutionRoute right after the statuses-presence check, before assertAgentClaimableStatuses, the workerId check, touchWorker and any waiter. findMatchingTask passes the route to executionAdmissionRefusal for both the own-task match and the pool. The claim hint and the timeout hint spread routeArg. executionRoute.test.ts W1-W4 and I2 pin this behavior.

DoD 2, then the one verification run.
(a) No sync was owed. Rows 7d3428d1 (395172f0), 34e42a0a (6ded0c93) and 55a5a9f9 (6272d308) each landed their own docs/MCP_SERVER.md hunk: get_commit_scope's workerId comment, propose_rail's GLOBAL-lists paragraph, and request_replan's Returns and sessionHandoff text. Write 'none was owed', with the three shas, in the completion summary.
(b) From your task checkout's root, run the three checkRefs once, joined with ' && '. The byte-exact command is in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-a024/verification-command.txt (1043 chars).

[3] fails if any byte outside the two sections differs from the merge-base copy (B = merge-base HEAD ${MOE_LAND_TARGET:-HEAD}), or if `git diff --check` finds whitespace errors.

(1) INVALID_INPUT: util/claimEligibility.ts parseExecutionRoute calls invalidInput('executionRoute', "must be 'vm' when present"). Check where it runs in claimNextTask.ts (after readProcessIdentity, before the project-loaded check and any write) and in waitForTask.ts.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights: The route marker can only refuse, and it is checked after readiness. verified-local is never ready today (docs/baselines/cq-m06/README.md), so every claim of a strict row fails EXECUTION_PROFILE_NOT_READY first, and EXECUTION_ROUTE_REQUIRED is latent until readiness holds. The docs must state this ordering, or a reader will expect the route error today. claim_next_task and wait_for_task share one predicate (util/claimEligibility.ts) by design, as the anti-spin rule, so the wait text says the same predicate applies and the wait skips rather than raises.

A concurrent docs row may land in claim_next_task's Notes (task-6cf09180's possible firstClaimAt/fileCollision sync). Worktree merge-tree handles disjoint hunks, so stay on the named lines. QA on the control checkout: checkRef [3] is vacuous there (B = HEAD), so diff <sha>^..<sha> by hand (mem:decision-doc-row-checkrefs-worktree-mode).
